claims.statement: Publisher presents Operation Paperclip as an investigation of postwar specialist recruitment and its ethical tradeoffs.
Publisher presents The Pentagon’s Brain as a history of DARPA; listed May 2026 date belongs to this edition.
Neufeld criticizes accuracy, balance and notes while acknowledging readable presentation and newly developed sources; the review is not a book-wide disproof.
claims.sourceLocator: Quest 21(3), partial printed p.51; PDF index2, parsed text

claims.statement: Open Road’s visible author and book pages attribute Blowback, Science of Coercion and The Splendid Blond Beast to Christopher Simpson.
Publisher frames The Splendid Blond Beast as an argument connecting economic/state interests, genocide and postwar accountability.
UC Press presents Deep Politics and the Death of JFK as Scott’s challenge to prevailing assassination explanations and interpretation of surrounding policy structures.
UC Press presents The Road to 9/11 through Scott’s analysis of secrecy, private wealth and foreign policy.
The August 1946 memorandum and enclosure describe recruitment policy and a Nazi-participation screening exclusion; they do not establish compliance for individual recruits.
NARA cautions that names appearing in released files do not establish involvement in wrongdoing.
